## Overview
Develop a comprehensive collection of examples demonstrating calculus operations involving the indeterminate I, including differentiation, integration, limits, and series.

## Tasks

### Differentiation Examples
- [ ] Basic derivatives with I
  - [ ] d/dx(I) = 0
  - [ ] d/dx(xI) = I
  - [ ] d/dx(I²) = 0 (since I² = -1)
- [ ] Product rule with I
- [ ] Quotient rule with I
- [ ] Chain rule with I
- [ ] Implicit differentiation involving I

### Integration Examples
- [ ] Basic integrals with I
  - [ ] ∫I dx = Ix + C
  - [ ] ∫xI dx = (x²/2)I + C
- [ ] Integration by parts with I
- [ ] Substitution with I
- [ ] Definite integrals with I
- [ ] Improper integrals involving I

### Limits
- [ ] Limits of expressions with I
- [ ] L'Hôpital's rule with I
- [ ] Limits at infinity with I
- [ ] One-sided limits

### Series and Sequences
- [ ] Taylor series with I
- [ ] Power series involving I
- [ ] Geometric series with I
- [ ] Convergence tests for I-series

### Multivariable Calculus
- [ ] Partial derivatives with I
- [ ] Gradient of I-valued functions
- [ ] Multiple integrals with I
- [ ] Vector calculus with I

### Special Functions
- [ ] Exponential with I: e^(Ix)
- [ ] Trigonometric relations with I
- [ ] Logarithms involving I
- [ ] Special function evaluations

### Applications
- [ ] Physics problems with I
- [ ] Geometry applications
- [ ] Optimization with I constraints
- [ ] Differential equations with I

### Interactive Examples
- [ ] Jupyter notebooks
- [ ] Step-by-step solutions
- [ ] Visualizations (where applicable)
- [ ] Interactive widgets

### Documentation
- [ ] Create example gallery
- [ ] Organize by difficulty

- [ ] Include common pitfalls

### Verification

## Example Categories

### Beginner
Simple, introductory examples that demonstrate basic concepts

### Intermediate
More complex examples involving multiple techniques

### Advanced
Sophisticated examples showing deep interactions with I

### Research
Novel examples pushing boundaries of I-calculus

- Comprehensive coverage of I-calculus topics

## Notes
These examples will serve as both documentation and test cases for the calculus functionality. They should be pedagogical and demonstrate the unique properties of working with the indeterminate I.
